acceptance: A canonical codex/<task> branch remains accepted without consulting the Start Receipt.
When a Start Receipt records a non-canonical branch, closure accepts only the exact recorded branch currently checked out.
Closure still verifies the merged PR head branch and exact head SHA, synchronizes the discovered default branch fast-forward-only, proves remote branch absence, and deletes the local retry identity.

Regression tests cover canonical branch acceptance, exact recorded non-canonical branch acceptance, and mismatch rejection; no Weekly Radar runtime, data, pending, Secret, or production behavior changes.
guidelines: Keep canonical Work Item branches named codex/<task>.

intent.problem: The merged Weekly Radar Work Item used the branch wi/weekly-radar-cli-output-guard and recorded that exact identity in its immutable Start Receipt. ai-close-work-item rejects it before inspecting the already merged PR, so the Work Item cannot complete its required lifecycle even though all implementation and PR evidence is valid.
constraints: Canonical new Work Items must continue to use codex/<task> branches.
The compatibility path may use only the exact branch recorded in the immutable Start Receipt for the same task.
Do not weaken merged PR head SHA ownership, base synchronization, remote branch absence, or local branch deletion checks.
Do not rewrite the predecessor archive, change data or pending refs, read Secrets, or trigger production from this Work Item.
intent.rationale: The Start Receipt is the authoritative identity for the already-created Work Item. Accepting that exact recorded branch lets the existing closure checks run to completion without treating arbitrary branch names as trusted or changing the canonical branch policy for future Work Items.
